subject: AI & Agents
title: The AlexNet Moment
description: Learn The AlexNet Moment in one minute.

hook.text: September 2012. A deep neural network smashes the ImageNet competition. The error rate drops by 10%.

buildup.text: AlexNet used deep convolutional layers trained on GPUs — techniques others had dismissed.

discovery.text: It proved deep learning could outperform all hand-crafted feature engineering approaches.

twist.text: The winning team had just three people: Krizhevsky, Sutskever, and Hinton.

climax.text: Within a year, every top ImageNet entry used deep learning. The paradigm shifted overnight.

punchline.text: Three researchers, two GPUs, one revolution.

quiz.question: What did AlexNet prove about deep learning?
options: Deep neural networks could vastly outperform hand-crafted approaches
GPUs were useless for AI training

details.summary: In 2012, AlexNet won the ImageNet competition by a massive margin using a deep convolutional neural network trained on GPUs. This single result reignited the entire field of deep learning.
details.whyItMatters: AlexNet proved that deep learning with GPUs could dramatically outperform traditional computer vision. It triggered the deep learning revolution that drives virtually all modern AI breakthroughs.
takeaways: AlexNet won ImageNet 2012 with a 10 percentage point lead
It proved GPUs could train powerful deep neural networks
The result sparked the modern deep learning revolution

faq.question: Why was AlexNet's ImageNet victory so important?
faq.answer: Previous approaches used hand-crafted features and improved incrementally. AlexNet slashed the error rate from 26% to 16% using neural networks. It proved deep learning was fundamentally superior for vision tasks.

faq.question: What role did GPUs play in AlexNet's success?
faq.answer: GPUs could perform the massive parallel computations that training deep networks requires. AlexNet used two NVIDIA GPUs, demonstrating that affordable hardware could power breakthrough neural network training.
